summary: The Network Service Header is added to packets or frames to realize Service Function Paths. It also allows metadata to be exchanged along those paths. NSH is the encapsulation needed for the service function chaining architecture.

eli5.summary: It is a ticket attached to a packet telling it which services, such as a firewall, to visit in what order, plus notes to share along the way.

questions: what is the network service header
what is the nsh service index
how does nsh service function chaining work
subtitle: A small header that tells a packet which chain of services to visit, and carries notes for them along the way.

tldr.problem: Services such as security, WAN acceleration and load balancing were tied to network topology and did not adapt well to virtualized, elastic environments where workloads and services move.
tldr.mechanism: A Service Classifier adds a Network Service Header to the packet. It carries a Service Path Identifier, a Service Index for the position in the path, and optional metadata. An outer transport encapsulation delivers it between service nodes.
tldr.outcome: NSH is the encapsulation required by the Service Function Chaining architecture of RFC 7665. It is meant for use inside a single provider's administrative domain, and the NSH must be stripped before packets leave.

today: RFC 8300 is a Proposed Standard that has been updated by RFC 9451; it has not been obsoleted. The RFC itself only says the NSH is the SFC encapsulation required by the architecture of RFC 7665.

sections.title: Why a Service Header
sections.content:
Service Functions such as security, WAN acceleration and server load balancing are widely deployed. Before the Service Function Chaining (SFC) architecture of RFC 7665, deployments were relatively static and bound to the network topology, and they did not adapt well to elastic, virtualized environments. The RFC lists three needs: moving Service Functions and workloads around, binding service policy to granular information such as per-subscriber state, and steering traffic to the right Service Functions.

The Network Service Header (NSH) is a new data-plane protocol that answers these needs. It wraps the original packet or frame and is itself wrapped by an outer transport encapsulation that delivers it to NSH-aware network elements. It is made of three parts: identification of the Service Function Path, the location within that path, and optional per-packet metadata.

The scope is deliberately narrow. The NSH is intended for use within a single provider's operational domain, and an NSH-aware control plane is outside the scope of the document.
sections.eli5: Imagine a package that must pass through several inspection desks. The NSH is the label on the box saying which desks to visit and which one is next, so the road system does not need to know anything about it.

sections.title: NSH Layout and Metadata Types
sections.content:
An NSH is a 4-byte Base Header, a 4-byte Service Path Header, and optional Context Headers. The Base Header describes the service header and the payload protocol, the Service Path Header gives path identification and location, and the Context Headers carry metadata along the path. A Service Classifier adds the NSH, and it is removed by the last Service Function Forwarder (SFF) in the chain or by a Service Function that consumes the packet.

The MD Type field says what follows the first two headers. With MD Type 0x1, a fixed-length 16-byte Context Header MUST be present; one that carries no metadata MUST be zero. The RFC does not define what those 16 bytes mean. A Service Function or SFC Proxy that does not know their format MUST discard the packet and log the event.

With MD Type 0x2, zero or more variable-length Context Headers MAY follow. Each has a 16-bit Metadata Class, an 8-bit Type, one unassigned bit and a 7-bit Length in bytes. Senders pad the metadata to a multiple of 4 bytes, and receivers round the Length up to find the next field. The Metadata Class gives a hierarchical namespace so that standards bodies, vendors and others can define their own types.
sections.eli5: The label has a fixed top part and then a pocket for notes. In one kind of label the pocket is always the same size. In the other kind it can hold any number of notes, each tagged with who wrote it.

sections.title: The Base Header
sections.content:
The Base Header is one 32-bit word. Version MUST be 0x0 in this revision, and a receiver that does not understand the version MUST discard the packet and SHOULD log it. The value 01b is reserved because existing hardware uses the first nibble after an MPLS label stack for Equal-Cost Multipath decisions.

The O bit marks an OAM packet, MUST be set for OAM packets, MUST NOT be set otherwise and MUST NOT change along the path. TTL bounds the number of SFF hops and is the primary loop-prevention mechanism. If no initial value is configured, the default of 63 MUST be used, and each SFF MUST decrement it by 1 before the forwarding lookup. A packet MUST NOT be forwarded if the TTL is 0 after the decrement.

Length is the total NSH length in 4-byte words. It MUST be 0x6 for MD Type 0x1, and 0x2 or greater for MD Type 0x2. Unassigned bits MUST be zero when sent and MUST be ignored and preserved by other elements. Next Protocol names the payload: the NSH does not alter the inner payload. Packets with an MD Type or Next Protocol a node does not support are dropped, and implementations not configured for an experiment SHOULD silently drop the experimental values.
sections.eli5: The first line of the label says which version of label it is, how long the whole label is, how many stops the box may make before it is thrown away, and what kind of thing is inside the box.

sections.title: The Service Path Header and Forwarding
sections.content:
The Service Path Header is a 24-bit Service Path Identifier (SPI) and an 8-bit Service Index (SI). The SPI uniquely identifies a Service Function Path, and participating nodes MUST use it for path selection. The SI gives the location within the path. The initial Classifier SHOULD set it to 255, and Service Functions or SFC Proxies MUST decrement it by 1 after performing their service. An SFF that is not the terminal SFF for a path discards any packet with an SI of 0.

The SPI alone cannot forward a packet. It adds a level of indirection between the service path and the network transport. The combination of SPI and SI selects a logical Service Function and the network locator used to reach it, and the logical function may be a set of equivalent functions, in which case the SFF distributes load among them. Each SFF maps the SPI to an overlay independently, so the network operator keeps the freedom to engineer paths with traffic engineering, QoS marking or ECMP. The RFC shows example mapping tables with next hops, transport encapsulations such as VXLAN-gpe and GRE, and weighted metrics, and says how the tables are learned is outside its scope.

Anyone viewing the NSH, for instance in a packet capture, can see which path a packet is on and where it is in that path. A service seen by a user can also be a collection of paths joined by re-Classifiers, which is the idea of a service graph.
sections.eli5: The ticket has a route number and a step counter. Each helper crosses off one step. Local post offices look up the route number and step to decide which road to send the box down.

sections.title: What NSH-Aware Nodes Do
sections.content:
NSH-aware nodes (Service Classifiers, SFFs, Service Functions and SFC Proxies) have four kinds of action. A Classifier MUST insert an NSH at the start of a path, with a valid Base Header and Service Path Header, and an SFF MUST remove it at the end. If a later Classifier re-classifies a packet onto a different path, it MUST replace the NSH with a new one and set the initial SI, copying the O bit, TTL and unassigned flags transparently. Metadata MAY be kept.

SFFs MUST use the Service Path Header to select the next Service Function or SFF, and drop a packet whose SPI and SI do not match a valid next hop. Service Functions MUST decrement the SI, and Classifiers MAY update Context Headers. An SFC Proxy acts for a Service Function that does not understand the NSH: it MUST remove the NSH before handing over the packet and MUST re-encapsulate it with the SI decremented by one when it comes back.

The fourth action is service policy selection. Service Functions derive policy decisions, such as permit or deny, from the NSH. The metadata can come from network nodes, from external systems such as orchestration platforms, or from Service Functions. It can be augmented by later Classifiers, or updated if the first classification turns out to be wrong, for example when traffic first labeled Internet is later found to be an attack. Because the SPI can encode a classification result, metadata can also change which path a packet takes.
sections.eli5: The first desk staples the ticket on, each helper crosses off a step, and the last desk takes the ticket off. If a helper decides the box needs a different route, it swaps in a new ticket with the same stop-count rules.

sections.title: Transport Encapsulation and Fragmentation
sections.content:
Once the NSH is added, an outer transport encapsulation forwards the packet to the start of the service chain. It creates a topologically independent services plane, and transit nodes simply forward the encapsulated packets without modification. The NSH is independent of the transport used, and the presence of an NSH is signaled by a protocol type or another indicator in the outer encapsulation.

The NSH and the transport header make the packet larger. Within a managed domain, an operator can make sure the underlay MTU is large enough to avoid fragmentation. The NSH has no fragmentation support of its own, so the transport encapsulation ought to handle it, and in no case would fragmentation duplicate the NSH header. When the NSH is carried in IP, IP fragmentation together with Path MTU Discovery (RFC 8201) is used, and an operator should make sure ICMP is not blocked. If the underlay cannot fragment, an error message SHOULD be logged when a too-big packet is dropped.
sections.eli5: The ticketed box rides inside a bigger delivery truck. The truck can be any kind, and if the box is too big for a road, the truck company, not the ticket, deals with it.

sections.title: Security and Trust Model
sections.content:
The NSH is not an end-to-end protocol. It is imposed by a network device on ingress to the SFC domain and removed at egress, so there is an underlying trust in the devices that impose, remove and act on it. All Classifiers, SFFs and Service Functions in an operator's environment are assumed to be vetted and maintained, which differs from the zero-trust model, and operators SHOULD monitor them continuously.

Domain edges are the main defense. Egress devices MUST strip the NSH, the transport encapsulation MUST be filtered at the domain edge, and ingress packets MUST be filtered too, so packets entering or leaving the domain with an NSH MUST be dropped.

The NSH does not mandate its own integrity protection. If an operator needs it, options include verifying that NSH values come from expected devices, using an outer transport with cryptographic protection such as IPsec (which MUST be used if protection is deemed necessary), or an integrity scheme built on MD Type 2 variable headers. Connectivity that crosses the public Internet MUST be secured at the transport layer. For privacy, metadata should be limited to what the path needs, subscriber-identifying information SHOULD be obfuscated, and encryption of metadata can be used where that is not enough.
sections.eli5: The ticket is only meant to be used inside one trusted building. Guards at the doors take tickets off boxes leaving and refuse boxes with tickets coming in from outside.

sections.title: IANA Registries and Codepoints
sections.content:
IANA created a new "Network Service Header (NSH) Parameters" registry with sub-registries for the base header bits, the version, the MD Types, the MD Class, the IETF-assigned variable-length metadata types and the Next Protocol values. New MD Type values need IETF Review and new Next Protocol values need Expert Review.

MD Types 0x0 (reserved), 0x1, 0x2 and 0xF (experimentation) are defined. The MD Class registry assigns 0x0000 to the IETF Base NSH MD Class, 0xfff6 to 0xfffe to experiments and 0xffff as reserved, and no initial IETF-assigned metadata types exist. The Next Protocol registry is 8 bits wide, and IANA is to alert the IESG if half of the range is used. An IEEE Ethertype, 0x894F, has been allocated for NSH.
sections.eli5: There is an official list that gives every kind of label and every kind of box content its own number, so everyone writes them down the same way.

fields.name: O
fields.desc: Set for OAM packets; not modified along the path.

fields.name: TTL
fields.desc: Maximum SFF hops; default initial value 63.

fields.name: MD Type
fields.desc: Format of the NSH beyond the first two headers.

fields.name: Next Protocol
fields.desc: Protocol type of the encapsulated data.

fields.name: Service Path Identifier
fields.desc: Uniquely identifies a Service Function Path.

fields.name: Service Index
fields.desc: Location within the path; initial value SHOULD be 255.
